title: The Case of the Painted Buoys
story: Nico woke to find his orange lobster buoys painted a bright, cheerful purple, and now nobody on the pier can tell whose traps are whose. He swears you can see them from Portugal. Gus remembers selling paint to five customers at Mahoney's this week, and exactly one can of purple, but his famous knee forecasts rain, not faces. Who turned Nico's buoys purple?

texts: Of Yusuf and the buyer of the white paint, one picked up the sponge and the other picked up the spray can.
The customer with the rag spent less than the buyer of the purple paint.
Of the buyer of the black paint and the customer who spent $14, one is Yusuf and the other is Della.
Enzo spent more than the customer with the roller.
The customer who spent $10, the customer who spent $14, Marta, and Yusuf are four different customers.
The customer with the spray can bought either the black or the yellow paint.
Of Yusuf and the customer with the wide brush, one bought the black paint and the other bought the purple paint.
Yusuf spent two dollars less than the customer with the wide brush.
The customer with the roller spent more than the buyer of the teal paint.
